title: Abraham Lincoln
subtitle: A poor boy from a small wooden house, and the president who ended slavery.
description: An A1 reading and listening text on Abraham Lincoln: his childhood, his books, the Civil War and the end of slavery in the United States.
source: authored for this site; no source document
passage: Abraham Lincoln was born in 1809 in a small wooden house in Kentucky. The house had one room. The family was poor.
Lincoln went to school for less than one year. But he loved books. He read in the evening, next to the fire, after a long day of work.
He was very tall — one meter ninety-three. People remembered him for that, and for his quiet voice.
Lincoln worked as a lawyer. Then he went into politics, and in 1860 Americans chose him as president.
At that time, some states in the south had slavery. Black people there were not free. They worked for no money, and they were bought and sold.
Eleven southern states did not want Lincoln as president. They left the country, and a terrible war started. We call it the Civil War. It was Americans against Americans.
In 1863, in the middle of the war, Lincoln said that enslaved people in the southern states were free.
The war finished in April 1865. The United States was one country again. Later that year, a new law ended slavery everywhere in the country.
Five days later, a man shot Lincoln in a theater in Washington. The president died the next morning.
Today you can see Lincoln on the five-dollar bill, and in a big white building in Washington, D.C., where he sits in a chair and looks at the city.

items.prompt: What was Lincoln's first house like?
items.explanation: A small wooden house in Kentucky with one room. The family was poor.

items.prompt: How long did Lincoln go to school?
items.explanation: Less than one year — but he read a lot at home.

items.prompt: When did Americans choose Lincoln as president?
items.explanation: They chose him in 1860. 1809 is the year he was born.

items.prompt: Why did eleven southern states leave the country?
options: They did not want Lincoln as president
items.explanation: They did not want Lincoln as president, and they wanted to keep slavery.
A war between two groups inside one country. The text says: Americans against Americans.

items.prompt: What happened five days after the war finished?
items.explanation: A man shot him in a theater in Washington, and he died the next morning.

exercises.title: True or False?
exercises.instructions: Decide if each sentence is true or false.

items.explanation: False — the text says the family was poor.
True — he read in the evening, next to the fire.
False — he was very tall: one metre ninety-three.
True — it finished in April 1865.
False — the country was one again, and later that year a new law ended slavery everywhere.

exercises.title: Words from the Text
exercises.instructions: Choose the word that matches the meaning.

items.prompt: A person whose job is the law is a ___.
items.explanation: A lawyer. Lincoln worked as a lawyer before politics.

items.prompt: A war between two groups inside one country is a ___ war.
items.explanation: A civil war.

items.prompt: Kentucky, Virginia and Texas are American ___.
items.explanation: States. There are fifty of them.

items.prompt: A person with very little money is ___.
items.explanation: Poor.

items.prompt: Five dollars on paper is a five-dollar ___.
items.explanation: A bill. In American English, paper money is a bill.

exercises.title: Complete the Summary
exercises.instructions: Complete each sentence with the correct word.

items.prompt: Lincoln was born in ___ in a small wooden house.
items.explanation: 1809. He became president in 1860 and died in 1865.

items.prompt: He read books next to the ___ after work.
items.explanation: Next to the fire — the house had no electric light.
Southern states, where slavery was legal.

items.prompt: In 1863 Lincoln said that enslaved people in the south were ___.
items.explanation: Free.

items.prompt: A man shot Lincoln in a ___ in Washington.
items.explanation: In a theater, five days after the war finished.

discussion: Lincoln read books after work every evening. When do you read or study?
Why do you think Lincoln is on American money?
Is there a person from your country's history that everybody knows? What did this person do?
